title: Canonical device security model
description: Vendor-neutral security model produced by the mapping engine for one device. Every leaf is a {value, state, evidence} triple; every collection carries its own state. Rule assertions read values through the evaluator's projection, so `services.ssh.version` in a rule means `services.ssh.version.value` here. Annotations: x-path is the canonical field path used by packs and rules (never rename one; adding is free); x-absent is the default absent-semantics a vendor pack should start from; x-key is the attribute a pack scope like `interfaces[{name}]` joins on. Field descriptions are ranking text for the suggestion service.

hostname.description: The name the device calls itself, as set in its configuration.

vendor.description: The manufacturer of the device, such as Cisco or Juniper.

os_family.description: The operating system family running on the device, such as IOS, NX-OS or Junos.

os_version.description: The software release version of the device operating system.

model.description: The hardware model or platform name of the device.

serial.description: The chassis serial number of the device.

enabled.description: Whether remote login over the encrypted Secure Shell protocol is turned on.
enabled.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

version.description: Which SSH (Secure Shell) protocol version the device accepts; version 1 is cryptographically broken and version 2 is required by hardening guides.

timeout.description: How many seconds the device waits for an SSH client to finish logging in before dropping the connection.
timeout.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

max_auth_tries.description: How many authentication retries (failed password attempts) an SSH client is allowed before the connection is closed.
max_auth_tries.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

enabled.description: Whether remote login over unencrypted Telnet, which sends passwords in clear text, is turned on.
enabled.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

enabled.description: Whether the built-in web management server is reachable over unencrypted HTTP.
enabled.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

enabled.description: Whether the built-in web management server is reachable over encrypted HTTPS.
enabled.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

enabled.description: Whether centralised authentication, authorisation and accounting is switched on instead of only local line passwords.
enabled.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

algorithm.description: How the privileged-mode administrator password is stored: plaintext, reversibly encoded, or hashed and with which hash function.

password_min_length.description: The shortest password the device will accept when a local password is set.
password_min_length.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

present.description: Whether a warning message is shown to users before they log in, such as an authorised-use-only notice.
present.x-absent: default false when the banner command is absent

local_users.description: User accounts defined directly on the device rather than on an authentication server.
local_users.x-absent: empty with state mapped when the reader parsed the file and found no user definitions

name.description: The login name of a locally defined user account.

privilege.description: The privilege level granted to a local user account; higher means more administrative power.
privilege.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

password_algorithm.description: How a local user's password is stored: plaintext, reversibly encoded, or hashed and with which hash function.

idle_timeout.description: How many seconds an idle administrative session stays open before the device logs it out; 0 means never.
idle_timeout.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

enabled.description: Whether the device records system and security events at all.
enabled.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

level.description: The least severe event the device logs, its syslog trap level: a severity from 0 (emergencies only) through 6 (informational) to 7 (debugging, everything).
level.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

buffered_enabled.description: Whether log messages are kept in a memory buffer on the device itself.
buffered_enabled.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

servers.description: Remote syslog servers the device sends its log messages to.
servers.x-absent: empty with state mapped when the file was parsed and no log server is configured

items.description: Address or hostname of one remote log server.

authenticate.description: Whether the device only accepts time from clock servers that prove their identity with a shared key.
authenticate.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

servers.description: Network time servers the device synchronises its clock from.
servers.x-absent: empty with state mapped when the file was parsed and no time server is configured

items.description: Address or hostname of one time server.

version.description: The weakest SNMP monitoring protocol version the device answers; versions 1 and 2c send the community password in clear text.

traps_enabled.description: Whether the device pushes unsolicited alert notifications to a monitoring station.
traps_enabled.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

communities.description: SNMP community strings, the shared passwords monitoring stations use to read or change settings.
communities.x-absent: empty with state mapped when the file was parsed and no community is configured

string_redacted.description: A community password with its secret masked at ingest; kept only so communities can be told apart and well-known defaults like public can be flagged.

access.description: Whether a community may only read settings or may also change them.
access.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

interfaces.description: The physical and logical network ports on the device.
interfaces.x-absent: unknown; a device with no parsed interfaces is never treated as having none

name.description: The name of a network port, such as GigabitEthernet0/1.

shutdown.description: Whether a network port is administratively disabled.
shutdown.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

description.description: Free-text label an administrator attached to a network port.

proxy_arp.description: Whether a port answers address-resolution requests on behalf of other hosts, which can let traffic bypass intended routing.
proxy_arp.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

ip_redirects.description: Whether a port sends ICMP redirect messages telling hosts to use a different router.
ip_redirects.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

unreachables.description: Whether a port replies with ICMP destination-unreachable messages, which can reveal network layout to a scanner.
unreachables.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

switchport_mode.description: Whether a switch port carries a single VLAN, carries many VLANs as a trunk, negotiates its mode automatically, or is a routed port.
switchport_mode.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

access_vlan.description: The VLAN number a single-VLAN access port is placed in.
access_vlan.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

vty_lines.description: Virtual terminal lines, the slots remote administrators log in through over SSH or Telnet.
vty_lines.x-absent: unknown; a device with no parsed login lines is never treated as having none

name.description: Identifies a group of remote login lines, such as vty 0 4. Added in v1 as the join key the mapper needs.

transport_input.description: Which remote login protocols are allowed to connect on a group of remote login lines.
transport_input.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

access_class.description: The name of the access list restricting which source addresses may log in on a group of remote login lines.
access_class.x-absent: default null meaning no source restriction

exec_timeout.description: How many seconds an idle remote login session stays open before it is closed; 0 means never.
exec_timeout.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

lists.description: Access control lists, named sets of rules that permit or deny traffic.
lists.x-absent: empty with state mapped when the file was parsed and no access list is defined

name.description: The name or number identifying an access control list.

entries.description: The ordered rules inside one access control list.
entries.x-absent: empty with state mapped when the list exists but has no rules

seq.description: The sequence number giving a rule's position inside an access control list.

action.description: Whether a rule in an access control list allows or blocks matching traffic.

cdp_enabled.description: Whether the device advertises its identity and software version to neighbours with Cisco Discovery Protocol.
cdp_enabled.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

lldp_enabled.description: Whether the device advertises its identity to neighbours with the standard Link Layer Discovery Protocol.
lldp_enabled.x-absent: pack-declared default for the OS version range, otherwise unknown

state.description: mapped: read from a config line. defaulted: no config line backs the value; it is the pack's declared default for an absent line, a platform constant, or operator-supplied (see evidence.source). unknown: we cannot say; rules requiring this field return NOT_DETERMINED.

line.description: 1-based source line number; null for a defaulted value, which has no line.

source.description: Where a value with no config line came from. platform_constant: the vendor pack states a fact true of every device of this platform. operator: supplied by the person running the scan. Omitted: read from config, or the pack's declared default for an absent line.

collection.description: state describes the list as a whole. An empty list with state unknown means we failed to read it and must yield NOT_DETERMINED, never a vacuous PASS.

complete.description: False when the visible items are real but more may exist that we could not read (e.g. inherited configuration). Omitted means true. Only a read list can be incomplete.
